summary_html: Agency **files a court petition** to open a **dependency** (or similar) case. Federal funding frameworks (IV-E/ASFA) link court oversight, reasonable-efforts findings, and permanency timelines to downstream actions.
authority_html:
- **ASFA / SSA Title IV-E** — court findings; timelines; permanency planning  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal review of court/agency performance measures

primary_citations.citation_text: New York - N.Y. Soc. Serv. Law § 411 et seq. (Child Protective Services Act – reporting requirements)
New York - Family Court Act Article 10 (Abuse/Neglect juvenile proceedings)

New York - N.Y. Soc. Serv. Law § 422 (Statewide Central Register; for investigations commenced on or after January 1, 2022 a report is indicated only where there is a fair preponderance of the evidence that the alleged abuse or maltreatment occurred, and the burden of proof at the subject's fair hearing is on the child protective service which investigated the report)

provisions_triggered.name: Due Process / Law of the Land

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: Answering certified questions from the Second Circuit, the Court of Appeals held that a child's exposure to domestic violence does not alone establish neglect or justify removal, that neglect requires a preponderance showing of actual or imminent impairment caused by the parent's failure to exercise a minimum degree of care, and that emergency removal without a court order under Family Court Act § 1024 is permissible only where the danger is so urgent that there is no time to obtain an ex parte order.
key_cases.relevance: Nicholson defines the two elements (impairment or imminent danger, plus failure to exercise a minimum degree of care) an article 10 petition must plead and prove.
key_cases.quote: emergency removal is appropriate where the danger is so immediate, so urgent that the child's life or safety will be at risk before an ex parte order can be obtained

key_cases.holding: Affirming findings of abuse and an order of supervision, the Court held that Family Court Act § 1046(a)(ii) creates only a rebuttable presumption shifting the burden of going forward to the respondents, while the burden of proving abuse by a preponderance always remains with the petitioning agency.
key_cases.relevance: Agencies filing article 10 petitions may rely on § 1046(a)(ii) but retain the burden of persuasion throughout.
key_cases.quote: The establishment of a prima facie case does not require the court to find that the parents were culpable; it merely establishes a rebuttable presumption of parental culpability

key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed abuse findings in two proceedings, holding that as amended Family Court Act § 1046(a)(vi) permits a child's out-of-court statements to be corroborated by any other evidence tending to support their reliability, including validation testimony by a qualified expert and the cross-corroborating statements of other child victims.
key_cases.relevance: Agencies petitioning on the strength of a child's disclosures must be prepared to supply corroboration meeting this standard.
key_cases.quote: As amended, section 1046 (a) (vi) states a broad flexible rule providing that out-of-court statements may be corroborated by "[a]ny other evidence tending to support" their reliability

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit
key_cases.holding: In an action arising from an infant's death and the ensuing child-protective proceeding, the Second Circuit held that agency lawyers who initiate and prosecute child-protective petitions have absolute immunity, that caseworkers have only qualified rather than absolute immunity, and that qualified immunity nonetheless barred the § 1983 claims against the caseworkers here.
key_cases.relevance: Agency attorneys who file and prosecute an article 10 petition act in a prosecutorial function and are absolutely immune.
key_cases.quote: The lawyer defendants are entitled to absolute immunity on plaintiffs § 1983 claims because they were performing functions analogous to those of a prosecutor

key_cases.holding: The Court held that an indigent parent charged with child neglect is entitled to assigned counsel and must be affirmatively advised of that right, so that a mother told only that she could hire and pay for a lawyer herself could not validly waive counsel or admit the petition, and it remitted the matter to Family Court for a new adjudicatory and dispositional hearing with counsel.
key_cases.relevance: This is the foundational New York holding that filing an article 10 petition against an indigent parent triggers an enforceable right to assigned counsel, the right later extended to effective assistance in Matter of Parker J.
key_cases.quote: to be relinquished to the State without the opportunity for a hearing, with assigned counsel if the parent lacks the means to retain a lawyer

key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed findings of severe abuse and termination of parental rights, holding that the Adoption and Safe Families Act amendments applied to the pending proceedings, that the agency was properly excused from exercising diligent efforts at reunification given the aggravated circumstances, and that derivative findings of severe abuse may be made as to siblings who were not themselves the direct victims.
key_cases.relevance: An article 10 petition may plead abuse or severe abuse derivatively as to every child in the household, so the agency need not allege a separate act against each sibling.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that an underlying finding that a child was abused may itself be derivative, even in cases other than those involving homicide or assault.

statutory_basis.citation_text: N.Y. Soc. Serv. Law § 422(5)(a), (8)(b)(ii) (fair preponderance of the evidence standard for investigations commenced on or after January 1, 2022; the burden of proof in the subject's fair hearing is on the child protective service which investigated the report)

timeline_requirements.starts_from: Receipt of the report (the investigation or family assessment response itself must commence within 24 hours)
A determination that the investigation did not find a fair preponderance of the evidence that the alleged abuse or maltreatment occurred (investigations commenced on or after January 1, 2022)
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in N.Y. Soc. Serv. Law § 422(5)

timeline_requirements.requirement_name: Request to amend an indicated report
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Notice to the subject of the report that the report is indicated
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in N.Y. Soc. Serv. Law § 422(8)(a)

notice_requirements.timing: In writing, no later than 7 days after receipt of the oral report
content_required: Rights of the subject of the report

statutory_basis.citation_text: 18 NYCRR 432.2(b)(3)(ii)(f) (after seeing that the children named in the report are safe, the child protective service must notify the subjects and other persons named in the report, in writing, no later than seven days after receipt of the oral report, of the existence of the report and the subject's rights)
